description: Spaghetti alle Vongole is a quintessential Italian pasta dish, celebrated for its simple elegance and fresh flavors. This recipe highlights tender Manila clams tossed with al dente spaghetti in a fragrant white wine, garlic, and chili sauce. It is a true taste of the Mediterranean coast, perfect for any seafood lover.

instructions.title: Prepare the Clams
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the Manila clams by scrubbing their shells and purging them in a bowl of cold salted water for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours. This helps remove any sand. Discard any clams that are open and do not close when tapped.

instructions.title: Cook the Spaghetti
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Add the spaghetti and cook according to package directions until al dente. Before draining, reserve about 1 cup of the pasta cooking water.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: While the pasta cooks, heat the extra virgin olive oil in a large, deep skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté gently for 2-3 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and lightly golden, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Steam the Clams
instructions.text: Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the cleaned clams to the skillet and pour in the dry white wine. Cover the skillet tightly with a lid and cook for 5-7 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until all the clams have opened. Discard any clams that remain closed.

instructions.title: Combine Pasta and Sauce
instructions.text: Drain the spaghetti and immediately add it to the skillet with the opened clams and sauce. Add half of the chopped fresh parsley and a splash of the reserved pasta cooking water. Toss vigorously to combine, allowing the pasta to absorb the delicious clam broth.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Continue tossing for another 1-2 minutes, adding more pasta water if needed to create a luscious sauce that coats the spaghetti. Season with freshly ground black pepper and a little salt if necessary (the clams and pasta water are naturally salty). Serve immediately, garnished with the remaining fresh parsley.

tips: Always purge your clams properly. Soaking them in cold, salted water for an hour or two helps them expel sand, ensuring a grit-free dish.
Do not overcook the pasta. It should be al dente when it goes into the clam sauce, as it will continue to cook slightly while tossing.
Reserve some pasta water! This starchy water is essential for emulsifying the sauce and creating a glossy, rich coating for your spaghetti.
